title: python dep-graph drops the module in 'from pkg import module' — blast-radius reverse deps undercounted (engine: ledger 18 recorded vs 47 real importers)
detail: prusik/discovery_plugins/python.py:23 records ImportFrom as node.module only, so 'from prusik import ledger' becomes an edge to bare 'prusik' and the submodule is lost. In this repo the cartographer (2026-10-25) measured ledger.py's real importers at 47 vs 18 attributable from .sprint/dep-graph.json. Every consumer of the reverse graph (blast_radius / plan-reach / fix-round fan-out lane / consistency predicted reverse-deps) inherits the recall gap for the most common Python module-import idiom — a false-confidence class: a change to a widely-imported module reads as low-blast. Relative imports (level>0) are also skipped entirely (documented follow-on). Suggest: for ImportFrom also emit '<module>.<alias>' per imported name (resolution already tolerates non-module names via the prefix walk), resolve relative imports against the file's package, and moat-test with this repo's ledger.py reverse count.

resolution.verify: CUR=$(prusik --version 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+' | head -1); [ -n "$CUR" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' '0.225.0' "$CUR" | sort -V | head -1)" = '0.225.0' ] && echo "1 passed: engine carries moat-proven fix fb-27ad79ae220b (prusik $CUR >= 0.225.0)"
